headline: Superintendent Skinner says he will retire when his contract ends in June, after seven more months of work.
summary: Skinner said he has thought about this since entering the final year of his contract, and he will keep working on district goals over the next seven months. He said progress depends on everyone in the district, not one leader. Community school managers also described their work at seven schools, including STEM Academy attendance rising from 93% to 96%. Members accepted the superintendent's reports on a 7-0 vote, and a motion asking for Apple records died for lack of a second.
decisions: Request for Apple emails and unit orders died for lack of a second, so it was denied.
Accepted the superintendent's reports 8.1 through 8.9 as progress reports, 7-0.
Approved the donation from the Justin J Watt Foundation to the Maury School, 7-0.
Approved convention and conference requests 10.1 and 10.2, 7-0.
Approved the donation of 14 sick days to teacher Taylor LeDuc, 7-0.
Motion to move the December 2nd and December 16th meetings to December 9th was withdrawn.
discussion: Superintendent retirement: Skinner said he decided after thinking about it since entering the final year of his contract. He said he will stay committed to the district's work over the next seven months.

Community schools program: Managers said they connected with 99% of students at STEM Academy and documented more than 8,000 connections with families. They also said a six-week family program will run between February and April vacations at the STEM and Moody schools.

HVAC and heating: The superintendent said the city has new boilers and roofs, with more repair projects planned. A member asked whether repairs were complete, and the superintendent said the city is confident about winter heat.
December meeting schedule: Central office said it could keep both December meetings. A member suggested giving the packet on the Monday after Thanksgiving, and the motion was withdrawn.
